source_context: Meister et al., TACL 2020 Algorithm 2 per-length pop budget and Section 4.1 Equation 6 stop-only extension to nonmonotone scores; also present in arXiv v5 (2022).
authorship: Curator-authored finite-tree illustration; not an audit or execution of the authors implementation.
upper_bound: Exact best descendant completion score for every remaining hypothesis; equivalent to score+U.
interpretation: Changing only stopping does not restore the comparison guarantee for arbitrary nonmonotone scores when a per-length budget can prune an as-yet-unexpanded superior hypothesis. This toy analysis does not challenge the monotone-score method.
limits: This implementation specializes a finite depth-three tree and stores complete hypotheses as incumbents instead of repeated EOS padding.
The optional monotonicity-based older-layer deletion is deliberately not used; the per-length limit alone produces the discrepancy.
All complete paths have the same length, ties do not determine the result, and successor-score increments can represent an additively decomposable nonprobabilistic scoring function.
A primary correction or stronger nonmonotonic algorithm could add conditions or change pruning; that remains a separate evidence check.
